intro: A daily reading for the metro, mood-pieces more than predictions. Refreshed each morning.

horoscopes.text: Energy you usually save for Thursday shows up early. You catch yourself enjoying the part you usually skip. Somewhere near the Lake Harriet bandshell. The kitchen, not the bar, is the right room tonight.

You move through the day like someone who knows where the shortcuts are. You take a longer route home and notice three things. Somewhere near the second floor of Magers & Quinn. Skip the screen. Read instead.
A page-turner of a Tuesday. You learn a new word and use it correctly. Put the phone face-down. Sleep finds you faster.
The first hour belongs to whoever you live with. You write a long message and only send the short one. Somewhere near a corner of the North Loop. Call your mother, or someone who is.
Today is the kind of day people remember you on. A friend asks for advice and your advice is useful. Outside, a sky the color of zinc. A long shower and an early bed.
You are correct about a thing you were almost wrong about. A meeting ends ten minutes early and you do not refill the time. Somewhere near the Walker sculpture garden. Tomorrow's bag, packed tonight.
You wake up gentler than you were yesterday. You forgive yourself for last week. Somewhere near the East Bank between classes. Light a candle. Read for ten minutes.
Quiet power, well held. A long story comes to a quiet conclusion. Sleep with the door closed. You earned it.
A morning that wants you outdoors, briefly. You realize you have outgrown a complaint. Outside, an early haze that burns off by ten. Forgive yourself the thing from Tuesday. Sleep.
The morning is for the slow build. Money behaves predictably. Two months of math holds. Outside, a sky the color of zinc. Tomorrow will still be Wednesday.

A weird connection between two old conversations clicks. You vote in the small election. It actually matters. Outside, a wind that smells like rain six hours out. You did the small revolutionary act. Now sleep.

A poem you read once comes back, half-remembered, helpful. A friend's small problem becomes your large one for an hour. That is love. Somewhere near the Lake Harriet bandshell. Sleep finds the people who let it.
